priorFinding.scenario: Producer opens final response path then serializes JSON; consumer waits only for existence and immediately JSON.parse()s it. A scheduler interleaving exposes empty/partial JSON.
priorFinding.actual: Both unmodified full runs exited 1 (first A-filesystem, retry B-command), each with SyntaxError before its observer receipt was recorded. Completed response files are valid JSON. Verbatim consumer counterexample deterministically throws SyntaxError while writer is mid-response.
priorFinding.expected: The response is consumed only after complete publication; all 11 default checks finish in the same run.
priorFinding.suggestedRepair: Atomically publish a complete response using a same-directory temporary file and rename, or an explicit completed-response protocol with a bounded read. Preserve real malformed-response errors and current failure history; add a publication-race regression, then rerun the full default suite.

findings.implementation: T-106 publish_response serializes into an exclusive same-directory scratch inode, flushes and fsyncs it, then atomically hard-links the complete inode to the final name without overwriting. The directory is fsynced after scratch cleanup. Current consumer remains strict and unchanged; no JSON-error swallowing or arbitrary wait was added.
findings.regression: Actual current publisher paused inside real json.dump after the first character; the verbatim current consumer polls while the writer is held, sees no final name, and consumes only after release. A separate invalid-final-receipt case still raises SyntaxError.
findings.oldCounterexampleInterpretation: Historical direct-to-final-path reproduction remains intact; it bypasses the repaired publisher and is not represented as proof of repair.

priorFinding.scenario: verify_cached resolves manifest.parent before checking links, reads manifest without lstat, and checks only terminal package/binary paths; directory components are not checked.
priorFinding.actual: download-directory-link, extracted-directory-link, manifest-link and cache-directory-link are accepted. Altered source URL, altered package, altered binary and terminal package/binary links are rejected. All linked targets in the repro are independent checker-owned copies; cryptographic pins were not bypassed.
priorFinding.expected: All linked cache/source/package/binary inputs are rejected before reuse, including ancestors and manifest; unchanged genuine cache may still be reused without downloading.
priorFinding.suggestedRepair: Validate the un-resolved manifest and all relevant path components; use no-follow/open-descriptor identity checks for the manifest, package and binary. Keep the fixed package/source pins and signed provenance. Add regressions for all four accepted link forms.

findings.implementation: Unresolved input components are traversed with openat-style dir_fd and O_NOFOLLOW; lstat/fstat identities and regular-file bounds are checked, ancestors remain open and their entries are rechecked. Manifest/package/binary are read through anchored descriptors. The pinned archive bytes are sent to dpkg stdin; immutable verified binary bytes are passed directly to stage_tool for the run copy rather than reopening the cache pathname.
findings.regression: Seven symlink forms (including the four reported forms), source/package/binary tampering, legitimate cache reuse without network, directory replacement before open, opened-cache-anchor replacement, archive snapshot and runner upload-staging snapshot are covered.
findings.cryptographicScope: The old finding demonstrated accepted symlink inputs, not a digest bypass. Fixed source/package/binary pins are unchanged.
